To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of carrier RNA to the cell lysates of limited and degraded DNA samples prior to robotic extraction using either the BioRobot® M 48 or BioRobot® EZ 1 resulted in a significant improvement in the recovery of DNA, and that this improvement was greater than that obtained by the addition of carrier to the organic extraction of the same samples.

the addition of carrier RNA to the cell lysates of low‐yield and degraded samples prior to extraction on either the BioRobot®EZ1 or BioRobot® M 48 substantially increases DNA yields and improves the detection limit for degraded samples.

robotic extraction of DNA from blood and semen samples using carrier RNA consistently produced higher yields than organic extraction, and that carrier RNA increased the recovery of DNA from limited and degraded samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving DNA extraction from low‐yield samples.
the optimization of robotic DNA extraction, with a particular emphasis on the use of carrier RNA to increase the recovery of DNA from low‐yield and degraded samples.
the optimization of robotic DNA extraction from low‐yield and degraded samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BioRobot® M 48 with carrier RNA is the most efficient method for extracting DNA from limited and/or degraded samples.

the addition of carrier RNA to lysates of degraded and low‐quantity samples, extracted by either the BioRobot®EZ1 or the BioRobot®M48, results in an increase in DNA yields, while the addition of glycogen postlysis is ineffective.
the addition of carrier RNA to cell lysate is beneficial for DNA extraction from limited and degraded samples using either the EZ1 or M48.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of carrier RNA to the cell lysates of limited and degraded DNA samples, extracted on either the BioRobot® M 48 or the BioRobot® Ez1, will increase the recovery of DNA.
the addition of carrier RNA to the lysis solution is a simple, effective method for increasing DNA yields from limited and degraded samples.
the BioRobots can extract low amounts of DNA from limited samples with the use of carrier RNA, but that the use of organic extraction remains the method of choice for obtaining the most DNA possible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of carrier RNA in robotic extractions is an efficient way to recover DNA from dilutions, limited, and degraded samples.
the use of carrier RNA can improve the recovery of degraded and low‐quantity DNA samples, and that robotic extraction can be an effective means for processing large numbers of samples.

the addition of carrier RNA to cell lysates during DNA extraction using the BioRobots®, particularly the EZ1, can dramatically increase DNA yield and sensitivity, especially for degraded or low‐yield samples.
